claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
High-pressure torsion introduces severe plastic deformation into AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
High-pressure torsion breaks down the original lamellar structure into ultrafine grains.
Controlled annealing after HPT promotes partial, controlled recrystallization.
Controlled annealing relieves internal stresses produced by HPT.
HPT followed by controlled annealing produces a fine, homogeneous, stabilized grain structure with a more uniform phase distribution.
The refined and stabilized microstructure balances work hardening and ductility.
HPT followed by controlled annealing improves the strength–ductility balance relative to the as-cast alloy.
HPT followed by controlled annealing may increase yield strength by approximately 15–30% relative to the as-cast alloy.
HPT followed by controlled annealing enhances ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The refined and stabilized microstructure improves creep resistance under extreme-temperature service conditions.
The refined and stabilized microstructure improves corrosion resistance under extreme-temperature variations.
Excessively aggressive annealing can cause grain growth and negate the benefits of HPT-induced refinement.
The benefits may be limited to temperature and loading ranges similar to those tested experimentally.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says HPT breaks down the original lamellar structure into ultrafine, homogeneous grains, whereas the boundary condition says the process must maintain the essential eutectic lamellar morphology. It is unclear how much lamellar breakdown is intended or compatible with the stated boundary.
